utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My apologies for starting a bit late. It's my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir, and good morning to you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can follow the proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. If at any moment there are problems with interpretation, draw my attention immediately, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand and there will be no problems. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My name is Jan Wubben, senior trial attorney for the Prosecution team, together with Ms. Patricia Sellers and Donnica Henry-Frijlink as our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I am Vasvija Vidovic, together with Mr. John Jones. I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. Together with us is our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, and our case manager Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you and your team. Let's go into private session for a few -- a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was that you? Let's deal with -- very briefly with developments since yesterday. I take it you have prepared for today a new list of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that the understanding is the following, and I just want to make sure, Madam Vidovic, that you have been kept informed, as you should, by the Prosecution, not that I doubt it. But for the record, since we are in a public hearing I want to address this. I was informed yesterday that Mr. Gow has recovered -- Professor Gow has recovered from his illness, that however he could travel here and be here with us on Wednesday but definitely has to be back in New York on Thursday. Of course I asked the situation what was the situation before, because is this something that happened after that he was informed that he was no longer going to be a witness or was it something he had to attend to in New York even beforehand. But that matter solved, my instructions to my legal officer was to show my preference. I did not at the time consult the other two Judges, but I was pretty sure this is not something they would disagree. My impression was it would be much better to have Professor Gow, Mr. Gow, to start and finish his evidence rather than to have him here one day, go back to New York, and then continue another day. So I told my legal officer to contact you back, to contact the Defence, to see what the position is on the part of the Defence. If that is going to be the case, in other words that Professor Gow is going to come later, how are we going to make good use of the rest of the week. I was informed that there was agreement between you that Professor Gow will testify after -- it has to be after November 20th. The reason is I will be returning from New York to here just before then. So that will be Professor Gow and you can fix the dates among yourselves. Make sure you know beforehand how long you require him in the courtroom, both of you. And secondly, I was informed that you have agreed to bring forward two witnesses - I won't mention the names but I don't think they are protected witnesses. The first two you have on the updated list, and that will be after Professor Koeijer or Dr. Koeijer with Madam Manas standing by in case she is needed to fill in blanks. If I have said something which does not tell you with what I have been told is the agreement between you, let me know, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, as we confirmed by the letter and also our latest overview, without naming of course the witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- Wednesday should be filled up the Doctorandus Koeijer and the order of the crime-base witnesses as projected, with the possibility that Ms. Racine Manas might be slotted in on Friday or on a Monday, whenever there is a gap identified and of course whenever we have a declaration, an additional declaration, prepared for -- to inform and update Defence counsel in due time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I thank you. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can confirm that we have agreed with the Prosecutor to have Dr. James Gow heard after the 20th of November, as you've said, because we don't think it would be right for us to start the cross-examination at one point and then to continue it only a month later. I also wish to confirm that we are prepared to cross-examine these witnesses as proposed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. The other thing I wanted to inform you about is that you will recall that during the -- I think the first or the second day of the trial, I referred to the expert Prosecution motion on delayed discovery that you are aware of and that you had made submissions on. We have -- the three of us, we have been informed that the information that we were expecting has arrived. It was filed yesterday on an ex parte basis by the appropriate unit of this Tribunal, which is not the Prosecution by the way. We are going to inform the Prosecution of the result of the investigation that was carried out and we should be in a position to decide this matter within -- by Friday at the latest, by Friday at the latest. That's number one. Number two is we are in the process of elaborating the decision on the protective measures relative to Witness C001 and of course with regard to the other witness as well. And third, but not least, is that we have drafted already the decision on the Prosecution motion to add exhibits -- to file more exhibits. I still have to consult with the other two Judges on whether there is complete agreement or not on this motion. We will be seeing it during the break and hopefully we would be in a position to decide it today. Having finished these preliminary matters, if there is nothing else you would like to raise at this point, Madam Usher will escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Fagel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And again my apologies for starting with you 25 minutes late, but again we had some business to deal with. Welcome back. May I just remind you in a courteous manner that you are testifying under solemn declaration which you don't need to repeat today. Please take a chair and your co-national, Mr. Wubben, will continue with his examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Wubben: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning. Your Honour, I will take up from yesterday the additional report. I will begin with this additional report of the 19th of July, 2004, and I'll ask Madam Usher to hand over P265.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My first question is, Doctorandus Fagel: Do you recognise this report?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise this report as the combined report I wrote with my colleague Jan Koeijer on which I wrote parts on the handwriting examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who signed for this report?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: The handwriting examination part I did sign.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why is this report signed by two examiners?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Because it involves two different kinds of examination, comparative handwriting examination and the document examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you receive the request for handwriting and document examination?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: The request was received on June the 18th, 2004.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your comment on the date on page 2, if any? If you can also observe that the date of the report is the 19th of July, and I notice that the date received -- well, you can comment on that.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I have to apologise for that. This is a typing error. The 24th of July should be 24th of June, 2004. My apologies again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that date, 24th of -- well, now June, that's referring to what date?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: The date when I received the exhibits from Mr. Nasir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you receive these documents?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: They were handed over to me by Mr. Nasir one by one, and I had to sign for the receipt of these exhibits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you work on those documents subsequently?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you start the examinations?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I started the first examination -- first inspection the same day but a more extensive examination might have been a few days later. I don't exactly remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you prepared the report following?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And signed for it?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you send this report, to what institute?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: The report was sent on July the 19th, 2004.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this report the same report that you sent to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, I have a general remark on the division of appendices between the report, because it was a little bit confusing for me the first time when I read this copy. I informed this morning also Defence counsel of it. Please notice that after Appendix 4, 1, 2, 3, 5, 4, there should be Appendix 5. But between Appendix 4 and Appendix 5, there is a reiterance, there is a copy, of Appendix 2 and Appendix 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So far you haven't helped much to clear the confusion. I think you have made it more confounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Again please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's start. Appendix 5 I have found. Appendix 5 is on ER -- sorry. It's on page which is -- which has an ERN number 03594742.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now we should file Appendix 4 presumably, now. Appendix 4, as I have it, is on the previous page and it is stamped Impressions on documents. Then before that on the previous page there is appendix 3 which is the featured in the stamp impression on documents. And then the previous page, what I have, is appendix 2, the last page, page 3 of 3 of appendix 2. That's what I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And before, Your Honour, before that appendix 2, isn't that starting again with appendix 4?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it starts with appendix 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's what I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- then you have appendix 3 again, then appendix 2, one page only of -- sorry. The three pages of appendix 2. And then I have the write-up of the institute and then appendix 1. So basically it's very easy. You start on appendix 1 where it is. You go right through appendix 4. Then you -- we take out what follows until appendix 5 and we should have it clear. Because the rest is repetition. So if you take --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: One --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If we take it out --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well, it has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You start from appendix 1 and you keep flipping the pages up to where you come to appendix 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Because, Your Honour, may I suggest not to take those out because these are all subsequently ERN numbers. So that's why my suggestion is to the Court is to decide --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see, I see, I see. I see. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you've made a point. The documents -- the appendices are replicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I want to clarify in advance. Whenever there is a confusion what ERN number, that might be caused by this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You got me with you. Is the same thing carrying in the B/C/S version or not. Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we shall simply follow the number of appendices, the page number, and the exhibit that is marked. That is how we are going to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. I think we can move --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can move.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will go now to the report P265, the page 5 out of 10 and page 1 first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave a general explanation, a general introduction, of the handwriting analysis yesterday during this trial, Doctorandus Fagel, as an expert; the same introduction applies to this additional examination. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make use of the same 35 reference signatures, the well-known K signatures, as referred to in your report from February 2004?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including the recognition yesterday of those reference documents?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you use the same reference numbers as such and the linked ERN numbers?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, since we have already mentioned these documents in detail yesterday, I would like to move to the questioned documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctorandus Fagel, I subsequently would like to show you the questioned documents, starting now with questioned 21. I will show them to you one by one and request your comment in order to confirm the recognition of each of them on behalf of your examination done as an additional examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please, Madam Usher, show the witness Exhibit P75. My case manager informed me that it should be on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctorandus Fagel, is this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctorandus Fagel, this document Q21, exhibit number P75, is this a document that you examined and that you referred to in the additional report as Q21? Please confirm, if so, with the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to tell from this copy, but yes indeed, it is the document number 02075810. And I examined the signature at the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I had the original document for this examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So subsequently the next document. I ask Madam Usher to show Exhibit P107, as it is Q22. Doctorandus Fagel, is this the document that you examined and that you referred to in the report as Q22? Please confirm with the ERN.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, I'm looking at a copy of the original document which I examined with ERN number 01787786. There's only one signature, so that's the signature I examined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The subsequent exhibit number P120 to be shown to Doctorandus Fagel related to Q23.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: This is again a copy of the original document I examined with ERN number 01787832. And I examined the signature at the right-hand side below the letter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, Exhibit number P158 referred to as Q24.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: This also is the copy of the original document I examined, ERN number 01239545. And I examined the signature below as Q24.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Followed by document exhibit number P263, document Q25. ERN 03557343. So, Doctorandus Fagel, may I ask you: Is this the document that you examined and that you referred to in the report as Q25? And also notice the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document or a copy of it which I also examined as a copy of -- it has ERN number 03557343. I examined the signature on it as signature Q25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Followed by document Exhibit number P177, questioned document number Q26.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is also a copy of a document which I also had available as a copy. It has ERN number 03720934. And I examined the lower signature as Q26. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Followed by Exhibit number P179, questioned document Q27. Is this a document that you examined and that you referred to in your report as Q27? Will you please confirm the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: This is a copy of a document I examined and also had only a copy available of it. It has ERN number 03720936. And I examined the signature on it as Q27.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Followed by document exhibit number P198, questioned document Q28. Doctorandus Fagel, is this the document that you examined as an expert and that you referred to in the report as Q28? Can you confirm the ERN number, please.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document or a copy of it of the document which I also had available as a copy. It has ERN number 03721234. And I examined the signature on it as Q28.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document number P200, P-2-0-0 related to questioned document Q29. Is this the document, Doctorandus Fagel, that you examined as an expert and that you referred to in the report as Q29? Include the ERN number, please.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a copy -- a document or a copy of the it the document I examined. It has ERN number 03721253. And I examined the signature on it as signature Q29.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Followed by Exhibit number P210 related questioned document Q30.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is also a copy of the original document -- no, I think it's a copy of the documents I examined which has ERN number 03721400. And I examined the signature on it as signature -- let's check, Q30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Q31 as related to exhibit number P219, please. 2-1-9. Doctorandus Fagel, is this the document that you examined as an expert and that you referred to in your report as Q31?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: This is the document or a copy of it of the document numbered 03721482. And the signature on it I examined as signature Q31.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you examined the original?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: No. I examined a copy of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this confirmation. Followed by exhibit number 220 related to the questioned document Q32.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this is a document or a copy of it the exhibit I examined. It is 03721483. I examined a copy of the signature as signature Q32.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Doctorandus Fagel, let me turn now to your analysis procedure and methods you used. What procedure did you use to examine Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. these questioned documents as related to you and observed by you prior in this testimony?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it's the same as yesterday but I analysed the features of the signatures, the line quality, the pressure variation, and the proportions and the shapes of the -- elements that can be distinguished within the signature and I compared them to the same features which can -- could be analysed in the reference signatures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also enlarge signatures on behalf of your examination, Doctorandus Fagel? To what extent? And why did you do so?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When necessary I looked at certain details of the signatures under stereomicroscope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's how you could show also in your report the enlarged signatures?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the main reason, but I think it's for a better view of the features in the signature for you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there been, in general, traces of forgery, copying, or tracing found with the signatures in general?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I did not find any traces of copying or tracing, certainly not in the original signatures. But of course in the copied signatures I couldn't see all the details well enough to exclude this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does a signature change by passage of age or time? In general; I already referred to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, you asked him that question yesterday and he gave us a very good answer to that and he explained all the variations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will skip that as well as the factors in general that influence the signatures, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me address directly, then, Appendix 2 for the evaluation of the questioned documents as related in the report P265. So now we'll be shown the groups of signatures one by one, starting with Appendix number 2. And I refer you, Doctorandus Fagel, to Appendix number 2, meaning for ERN number of my observation 03594732. Doctorandus Fagel, while giving your professional opinion --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can the video screen be turned on everywhere. Please, Your Honour, can you confirm that the video screen is turned on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, could you please repeat the ERN number because I'm not sure whether we are talking about the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Appendix number 2 of your --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you are referring him to Appendix 2, he may be getting confused in that the ERN number that you are referring to is of that particular page --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I see, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and not of the ERN number which you used for comparative purposes. That's why he is getting --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thanks for your explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you have understand me. You can proceed, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We are showing page 1 of 3 out of Appendix 2, the questioned signatures and I referred Doctorandus Fagel to this group of signatures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While giving your professional opinion, Doctorandus Fagel, regarding evaluation of the questioned signatures, will you please refer to this appendix and tell me how did you evaluate the signature on questioned document Q21, as indicated there, and please confirm also the ERN number. What characteristics did you identify in this document for comparison with the reference documents or signatures?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the signature was available in the original, and judging from the good line quality and the natural writing pressure variation this signature was written fluently and didn't find any indications of copying or tracing within the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And may I have your same observation and comment on signature Q22.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's the same as for signature Q21.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the ERN number, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And may I have your observation and comment on signature Q23, including ERN.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I have the same comments as for the previous two signatures and the ERN number is 01787832.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the signature Q24, Doctorandus Fagel, including the ERN number. Your comment, please, in your professional opinion.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, also for this signature which I also had in original, judging from the good line quality and natural writing pressure variation it was written fluently. I didn't find any signs of copying or tracing within the signature. The ERN number is 01239545.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will turn now to page 2 out of 3 of your Appendix number 2 in your additional report. May I have the same observations and comments, please, starting with Q25.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I only had a copy available of this signature and the copy was too poor to allow detailed examinations in the writing course and quality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ERN number, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Q26 is the next signature. Same observations.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same observation as for Q25. ERN number 03720934.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Signature Q27. May I have your comment and observation, please, and the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: These are the same as for Q25. 0372096 -- sorry. 0936.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And subsequent Q28 signature including the ERN, your comments and observations.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: ERN number is 03721234 and my observations are the same as for Q25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you, for the record, please repeat that observation.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That the quality of this copy is too poor to allow detailed examination of the writing course and line quality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we turn to page 3, Doctorandus Fagel, page 3 out of 3 of Appendix 2 and we can start with the signature Q29.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: The signature on ERN number 03721253 is also -- I only had a copy available of this and the quality was too poor to allow detailed examination of the writing course and line quality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Q30 signature.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: This signature on ERN number 03721400. I also only had a copy available of it and also in this case the quality was too poor to allow detailed examination of the writing course and line quality.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: ERN number 03721482, which I only had a copy again. And again the quality of this copy was too poor to allow detailed examination of the writing course and line quality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally Q32.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: ERN number 03721483. And again I only had a copy of this signature and, again, it was too poor to allow detailed examination of the writing course and line quality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as for this part subsequent I will turn to the final results per document. Doctorandus Fagel, what can you clarify in your professional opinion about the results of the handwriting examination of all the questioned documents?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: All the documents?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the design and general appearance of each of the four original questioned signatures, that's Q21 and including Q24 is consistent with that of the known signatures. This --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Known signatures. You are then referring to reference documents and signatures?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned and confirmed the K documents?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: So that might mean that the questioned signatures are either authentic signatures written by the writing of the reference signatures himself or they could be imitations of the signature. But when I compared the construction and proportions of the various graphic elements with the corresponds element in the reference signatures, I didn't find differences that might not be accounted for by the natural variation normally present in anyone's signatures. And besides, I note that before no indications of copying or tracing were found in these questioned signatures. Now, the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a question in that respect. How easy is it to find forgery indications? It's more a question in general.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it depends on the skill of the forger. The better the forger is, the less easy it is to find traces of forgery. But in most cases, especially when the signature is complex enough, is not too simple, there will be traces of forgery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's -- you mean by traces, indications?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Indications, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So first you would trace the indication, more or less, and then you conclude on forgery or not?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are several kinds of forgeries possible. Someone can try to imitate the form of the signature as exactly as possible from a model. In this case, often the writing movement will slow down and this can be seen in the line quality. It will be more -- there will be less variation in the writing pressure and there will be more tremorous lines and there will be pen lifts in places normally where they are not in the authentic signatures. Another kind of forgery is when a person doesn't mind too much about the exact form of the signature but tries to make more fluent one, fluent imitation, freehand imitation. In that case, there will be more deviations in the exact moving course of the writing line. So the differences will be of another kind of character.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And will be shown under the microscope or whatever examination method you adopt?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We compare the -- as I said, the -- in most cases you can see them by the bare eye. But because we compare the shapes and the proportions of the elements within the signatures, and there will be the most important differences which can be seen which we will point out on our observation forms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now turning to the copies available, and you already confirmed several questioned documents as being a copy available to you. Can you tell something from the results point of view in regard to this quality of the copies.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the quality of -- you mean the qualities of the signatures Q25 up to Q32?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these copies were, as I said, too poor to allow examination of the writing course and line quality in sufficient detail. And all I can say is as far as can be seen from the copies, the overall design of these signatures is consistent with that of the reference signatures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I will turn to the final conclusions for the questioned documents Q21 up to Q25 referring to page 5 out of 8 of your additional report P265. Please give me your professional opinion about document Q21 also known as P75 as exhibit.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the results I got when examining and comparing the signature to the reference samples, I concluded that it's highly probable that this questioned signature was written by the author of the reference signatures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again please, highly probable, what do you mean by this classification?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: It's the second-highest conclusion we give. The highest one is with probability reaching on certainty --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he explained the differences between the various categories yesterday. I don't think we need to go through this again. If he just confirms that his assessment is highly probable, we know exactly what he means by that because he told us yesterday. I don't think it changes from one report to the other. So -- and to be honest with you, again I would suggest that you pool together these first five documents, 21 to 24 or 25 -- 21 to 24, and you can ask one question in relation to the four of them. That would be the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Doctorandus Fagel, can you give me your professional opinion about the final conclusions you made on questioned document Q21, Q22, Q23, and Q24 as examined by you.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: For all these signatures I concluded based on the results I got that it's highly probable that these questioned signatures were written by the author of the reference signatures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reference signatures what numbers?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: K1 up to K35.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And please, your same conclusion, professional conclusion, on the signatures Q25 up to Q32.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the results I got when comparing these signatures with the reference signatures, I can only conclude that it's possible that these questioned signatures Q25 up to Q32 were written by the author of the reference signatures K1 up to K35.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Doctorandus Fagel, this completes my questions so far. Finally, do you have as an expert, Doctorandus Fagel, anything to add that you would like to tell the Trial Chamber to your testimony this morning regarding the additional report?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe -- it's also the same as I said yesterday: that once you note opinions concerning non-original signatures are expressed on the assumption that the non-originals examined are true and accurate representations of the original documents, and that furthermore if the original documents were available for examination, this might result for stronger opinions for the signatures involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I've finished, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben. Mr. Fagel, Doctor Fagel, you are now going to be cross-examined by Mr. Jones who is appearing for the accused together with Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Jones:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Fagel, I would like to start by asking you a couple of questions about the Netherlands Forensic Institute. We've all seen your reports. Let's get them in front of us. If we look on the first page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which report? The first one or the second one, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Both. The first page of both reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is just by way of clarification we see at the top right-hand corner Ministry of Justice. Do you have your report?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see Ministry of Justice. That's the Dutch Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the top left, that's the logo of the Dutch Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Netherlands Forensic Institute is part of the Dutch Ministry Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of Justice?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a relatively autonomous service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, it would not be correct then to say, would it, that the Dutch Forensic Institute is not a laboratory that is within a government ministry in the Netherlands. That would be incorrect?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That the Dutch --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, if someone were to say that the Dutch institute is not a laboratory that is within a government ministry in the Netherlands, that would not be a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the institute funded by the Dutch government?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that it is relatively autonomous. It is not independent, is it?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: It depends what you call independent --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's your choice of words. You didn't say "independent," you said "autonomous."

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: But we consider ourselves to be independent and not to be influenced by the government in our opinions we give on -- based on our examinations, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the institute is part of the Dutch Ministry of Justice, just to clarify?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you a couple of questions now about the Netherlands Institute for War Documentation, also known as NIOD.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help us about the state of that institute? Is it autonomous, independent, or part of the Dutch government?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I protest. This is an expert on handwriting. He can hardly be asked an opinion about the qualification of an institute like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see what this other institute is all about and then we'll see what the next question will be. If it is relevant I will allow it. If it is not relevant, we will not allow it. I know that the gentleman is not an expert on other institutes, but we don't know which institute Mr. Jones is referring.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: By way of explanation, Your Honour, it's a source of one of the documents as we saw with Ms. Manas. NIOD has actually supplied a document to be used in the Prosecution against Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see what this institute is all about and if the witness is in a position to answer it and it is relevant we will allow the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wonder if you could help us with that.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I am not aware of the source of these documents at all. And about the organisational aspects of the NIOD, they are a governmental organisation but I cannot -- I'm not sure about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does your institute do work for NIOD examining documents?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I know in the past there have been some examinations for the NIOD, among other things the diaries of Anne Frank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: In Srebrenica for the NIOD? I think you are referring -- there has been some examination. I was not involved with it, with a photo -- a film.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you weren't involved, that's fine. We won't pursue that as well. Now, a couple of methodological questions. There may be amateur forgers, but there are professional forgers as well.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact is if someone who wants to get away with forging a signature, someone who has the time, motivation, and expertise can do it, forge a signature and escape detection. That's a basic fact, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The more time someone has and the more skilled someone is, the better forgery he will produce, I expect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But you've --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the question was double-edged. The end part of it is -- it was suggested to you that with all these -- the combination of time and skill, then one can escape detection. So please address that aspect as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it's very probable that this can happen, but I cannot guarantee that it will never happen. But that's also why we don't give 100 per cent opinions, qualified opinions, like highly probable, and this probability bordering on certainty. It's also related to the complexity of the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've referred today to copying and tracing marks. Those are, are they not, fairly amateurish signs that someone is literally trying to trace a signature. The more professional way, surely, is to practice the signature until it has slightly the same appearance as the one which is being copied.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I think that will be the more professional way, yes; but until it has exactly the same time appearance, of course two signatures of the same person are never exactly the same. Tracing would be rather amateuristic indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I speak slowly it's because I'm waiting for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason why you won't find those marks with a seasoned forger is because it's become the movement of the forger, hasn't it? It's become virtually his signature when he copies a signature repeatedly and perfects his skill.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the tracing marks --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When someone isn't tracing and not copying, they've practiced the signature enough that they can do it, it becomes a habitual movement of theirs and therefore easy to redo.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one would expect -- attempts we have seen by forgers trying to imitate a signature fluently, especially as the signature becomes more complex, is that even if they are fluent there will always be deviations in the exact -- in the proportions and/or in the shapes of several elements within the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "always," but at the same time you've told us you can't always be sure that a signature is not forged.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot guarantee 100 per cent that the signature is not forged. But that is also why we don't give certainty opinions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if - just staying on this issue of someone who is repeatedly copying the signature - there would be fluency in that movement and therefore good line quality and natural pressure variation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but again then I would expect more differences of another nature in the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just staying with this a bit longer. Expertise and time and motivation, let's start with expertise. You've trained as a forensic document examiner for a number of years. You know what to look out for, tracing, copying marks. Presumably, someone could do the same course as you and know what to look out for.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But another thing is also to perform it because I may be a good handwriting examiner but I am a bad forger I found out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly for government intelligence agencies, let's say, or counter-intelligence agencies, especially in the enmity of war, it would be well within their capabilities, surely, to have someone trained to do that. If that is within your competence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you don't thing you are in a position to answer that question, please ask us to exempt you from answering. Because I wouldn't know, for example.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Feel free for any question to say it's not within your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: This.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in terms of motivation. You mention expertise. Motivation, in a way that speaks for itself. But that is that surely a factor whether a forgery would be successful, for example, if someone was trying to forge a million dollars, they would probably practise a bit more. They would be better at it, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Practice can always help to make it better, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or if some more important issue is at stake.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to refer to page 2 of your forensic handwriting analysis synopsis, which is in both reports. Probably -- well, either will do, but I'm looking at the February report and the page number is ERN number 03523863. Do you have that in front of you. There it's just a -- I'll wait until you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, Mr. Jones. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, not at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is really to summarise in effect what you've been saying. I'll read the passage. "The more successful a forger is in reproducing the precise writing movements of a real signature, the will less his own characteristics will be present in the final result and more difficult it will be to determine who produced the forgery." That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But then here still going to be traces or indications of forgery. Because I mean if someone is tracing a signature exactly, then there are no characteristic, no features of his own handwriting anymore in the signature. But because this remark has to do with the fact sometimes you get forged signatures of which it is almost sure it can be a real one. But then the question is: Has this signature been forged by that person. So we have to compare his handwriting characteristics. So this remark is to explain sometimes you cannot do this because if it is tracing, for example, there are no indications, no features of his own handwriting anymore left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here you only have signatures to go on, don't you? You're not comparing signatures with other writing.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: No, nor with writing of other persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which limits the conclusions you can reach on that point you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the question was: Have these signatures been made by the owner, by the person whose name is with the signature. That's another question then, that have these signatures been forged by this other person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there are stamps involved, as we've seen in this case, surely a good technique of a forger would be to attempt to cover the signature or as much as possible stamp, in order to conceal. Is that something you come across?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I protest, Your Honour. Stamps is another investigation and we will question Mr. Koeijer. As confirmed by Doctorandus Fagel yesterday, there are two examiners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, but Mr. Wubben, if I understood Mr. Jones correctly, and I think I have, what he is suggesting to the witness as a question is whether if one wants to make it more difficult to establish the authenticity of a signature, whether it would help by way of making it more difficult to impose, superimpose this stamp on the signature itself so the comparative analysis, the comparative examination becomes more difficult. This is the point that is being made.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour. I apologise for my remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I can say two things about this. In the first place, for the original signatures we could under the microscope still follow the writing course of the lines in spite of the stamps which are on it. Of course for the copies, this was not possible. Secondly, if there are any traces of forgery in a signature, it will be very hard to put the stamps in such a way. First you have to detect where these deviations are and secondly you have to place the parts of the stamp exactly on this place in the questioned signatures, especially if there is more than one deviation which normally is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I might add something. If it is just a photocopy you wouldn't be in a position to know which came first, whether it was the signature and then the stamps or the superimposed or whether it was the stamp first and then the signature on it. Because a photocopy wouldn't tell you, whereas an original would.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on the originals the ink can run together presumably if they are stamped and signed.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: The ink can run together. I think if the stamp was put down first and then immediately after when the stamp is still wet, there can be some -- I don't know the English word for it, but there can be some mixture, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just a couple more questions about methodology and the exactness of your results or otherwise. When we speak about DNA testing you can get numerical probabilistic results, one in a million chance, one in a thousand. That's not possible in your field, is it?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: No. Like in many other forensic fields it's not possible in my field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not as exact as DNA testing.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why you have six categories on your probability scale.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You use, starting from, and we can look at that. For example, in the February report I have ERN number 03523865. You start with "a probability bordering on certainty."

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just pausing there: You haven't found that with regard to any of the samples which were to be examined?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including those where you had the originals and you had the best specimen to work from?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you have highly probable, probably, et cetera. Just a question: Is it right that with your scale, you could in effect divide it down the middle, the top three of where it's more probable than not, the bottom three where it's more probable -- sorry, more probably not than it is specimen; and the bottom half where it is more probably not than it isn't. Is that right? The top three would be more than 50 per cent and the bottom less than.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly more than 50 per cent but there are a large area around 50 per cent which is inconsistent, in my opinion, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I phrased it badly. I'll put it this way: the top three you have a positive batch and the bottom negative. So that in fact highly probably is in the middle of your positive matches.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I think all probable, highly probably, and with probability on certainty are all rather high on the scale because these steps are not spread evenly along the continuum.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come back to that. Now, the numbers of samples you used and the quality, if I can ask you about that. You used 33 reference signatures which were taken in a few days in May 2001. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And two on the 11th of April, 2003.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I have to check this. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're comparing those signatures taken on the same few days in 2001 and 2003 with signatures from 10 or 11 years before.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First if I can ask you about spread of specimen signatures. I'm not sure if you use that term in your field. But surely for the specimen samples, ideally you would have a spread from 1993, 1995, 2000 to compare, not just two time periods. Is that right? It would be better.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: It would be better to optimise results, but it's not really necessary. If you find differences, it would be a good thing to try to get signatures from the same period. If you don't find significant differences, you might ask whether it's really necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a question of necessity, isn't it? Are you actually able to provide a comprehensive analysis of that difference, or would your conclusions only be preliminary as an expert?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand this question. Can you rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your profession where you have a spread like that, samples from 10 or 11 years ago and then 10 or 11 years later, two time periods, in your field wouldn't most experts say: "My conclusion can only be preliminary. I cannot give a definitive definite conclusion."

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you say that a document is probably not of the author, a questioned handwriting is probably not produced by a certain person, that's what we would call a forgery, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you are talking about handwriting in general?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, on your scale and let me give an example. If someone signs Dr. Fagel on a cheque and you didn't sign it, that's what we would call a forgery, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if this person has the intention to imitate my signature, it would be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we were to compare your signature on a signature on a cheque that you hadn't written, you would find it's not your signature, you would be veering towards finding that's not a forgery, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to read this. Could you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can explain it more simply. It's understanding what your scale means because your job is to find out if signatures are forged. If you do a report and you say this is probably not the signature of an author, isn't that what we would call a forgery?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Not in all cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're free to explain.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on -- someone may -- for example, there might be another person having the same name as I have and signed with the same name in good faith and someone else might say this is your signature and I say, that is not my signature. So this person didn't have the intention to imitate my signature so it's not a forgery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's a question of intent.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now leaving the time spread to one side, I can probably deal with this issue before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If you want to lead with it. How long is it going to take you?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Five minutes maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. Then I think we take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I would just have a question to the expert with regard to your scaling. In your conclusions you distinguish between highly probable, probable, and possible. But if I go to this general outline, Forensic Handwriting Analysis, you will distinguish between with a probability bordering on certainty, highly probable, highly probably, and probably. But there you do not have the category of possible. What is -- how would you -- where would you fit in, so to say, possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this list which I showed, it only showed only the so-called probability conclusions. But below there is another explanation where I explained when we use possibly or no opinion. And possibly would be between probably and probably not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a 25-minute break if that's all right with you, reconvening at five to 11.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I raise the issue of the order of witnesses. Dr. Koeijer is stand-by available, as he told me yesterday, but he's waiting for a kind of confirmation that he should be available at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I very much depend on Mr. Jones, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I think I'll be finished by 12.30 at the latest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I suppose 12.30 we come to the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Or the re-direct, and that might take about a quarter, I don't know. That depends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I would say -- I would suggest that you call the other expert Koeijer, Dr. Koeijer, be here at 1.00. Because we'll certainly at least deal with the initial part of his testimony of his witness. I mean, we were discussing outside possible questions from the Bench but I don't expect too much or many questions from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We will confirm to him that he should be available at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thanks. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Fagel, before the break we were about to pass on to the subject of the time difference between the specimen signatures and the questioned signatures. In that regard, I'd like to first start with your Forensic Handwriting Analysis synopsis at page 2 which I've got at ERN 03523863. And I'll just read what you say there and you can tell me if you agree. "The writing movement can be regarded as an interplay of submovements, each brought about by the muscles and joints participating in the writing movement." Is it right -- I take it from that that handwriting is a subtle interplay between minute musculature and psychology, affected by the mental state of the writer.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the musculature is driven, so to speak, by the brains and there can be influence by drugs and alcohol and even by severe emotions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By severe emotions. I was going to give some examples so you can see -- tell me if you agree. If you're under stress, the signature might be shakier?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you're physically weak, the signature may be weaker, fainter?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I know of examples -- people who are of old age which are -- have deteriorated motoric ability where the signature may look worse; let's state it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that even cold hands can affect a signature.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you proceed from the assumption, I take it, that the signature of someone doesn't change much after adolescence. That's what you told us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Signatures made under normal circumstances, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Normal circumstances. Now, would that assumption be correct in the following set of circumstances, and I'll put those circumstances to you: If when the signatures were taken the person was 25 years old, under siege, under savage pressure, and fighting a war, first of all, 10 years ago; and then now, different circumstances all together, different diet, different build, 37 years old. I'm not talking about a one- or two-year time difference, we're talking about more than a decade. Is that assumption still a safe one in your expert opinion?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think -- it depends on how the person feels under the circumstances rather than the circumstances themselves I think. So he feels comfortable --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's post-traumatic stress syndrome, for example. That would surely affect it.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether this will influence the motoric musculature or motoric ability. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For you it's a perfectly safe assumption that a person 25 years old, under siege in a war is going to have more or less the same signature 10 or 11 years later in a totally different set of circumstances.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're happy with that assumption?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: There might be influences, but it's also possible that there are no influences at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A final question on methodology before we come to the questioned documents. The reference signatures are a yardstick, aren't they? They are what you can use to measure the questioned signatures against. You have those in this case because Naser Oric provided them willingly and that's why you can use them.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so there's no dispute, the case signatures are those of Naser Oric, he's not hiding that fact.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's what they told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Otherwise you would be making comparisons in a vacuum.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your task is to see if the author of the K signatures could be the author of the Q signatures.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let's turn to your report. Now, the February report, first of all. You got 20 questioned documents, 14 available in the originals. I don't know if I need to say the numbers. I think we know what they are. Six available in copies, six in the copies are Q4, Q6, Q7, Q10, Q11, Q16.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with those ones, the copies, you can't look at the strike indent, can you?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: The what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The strike indent?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't look for copying or trace marks.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: No a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A limited extent?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, depending on the quality of the copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't analyse the ink of the signature or of the stamp. In fact, many important analytical features are lost.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Again, depending on the quality of the copy -- the number of features that are lost can be more or less large.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a fact, isn't it, that there's a lot more scope for manipulation of a copy, especially in this day and age with scanners and the like.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I made my reservation on the end of the report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. Even an amateur can cut off the bottom of one page, Tip-Ex out the line, and copy it.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but sometimes we can see it's done this way because when you do it this way there may be shadow lines when you make a copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sometimes --

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: And there may be some other indications of manipulation, but not always.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right, isn't it? Because of all these problems with copies many people in your profession would insist on examining originals, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We normally also ask for the originals if you get copies but sometimes they are not available. Then we make our opinion, the best opinion you can, with all the reservations we have to make and usually an opinion with lower strength than normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask for the originals in this case?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: It was clear to me from the beginning that they were not available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you worked with copies?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I stated in my report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were happy to express conclusions about copies?

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusions that I made, I'm happy with, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to your conclusions in your February report. I'm looking at page -- sorry I'll have to use the ERN page because it's all -- it's really exact. 03523856. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let's start with the originals. You've told us the originals are the very best documents to work from. You can do all the tests you need with originals. And with none of the 14 originals do you conclude with probability bordering on certainty that they are the same author as the reference signatures.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's see what you do say. Again on the same page you say: "The design and general appearances of each of the 14 original questioned signatures," I won't read out all the Qs, "are consistent be that of the known signatures of N. Oric. This means that the questioned signatures are either authentic signatures written by N. Oric himself or imitations of his signature."

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Imitations of his signature.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: At this phase -- this is my conclusion at this phase and then I continue to the other examinations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that. You told us yesterday, didn't you, that an imitation is mala fides? It's a forgery, as we call it.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in fact your results are consistent with all the signatures on the originals being forgeries.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: My first results, first preliminary conclusion is that because of the similarity in the general overall design, it must be based on the signature of Mr. Oric or a model of it. So it could be his own signature or someone else trying to forge his signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. We've got two possibilities.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's either by Oric or it's imitation.

utterances.speaker: WILHELMUS PETRUS FRANCISCUS FAGEL [resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
